posts.body_html:
Completely forgot to put together a thread for this population, so here it is! I absolutely love these genotypes, there's an enormous amount of diversity, and if I had to sum up the unique features of the population as a whole, I'd say they look like Okaloosa Co, FL leucos except these have a lot of red forms in the mix, quite a few albas (which are super hard to color up), and have quite a few individuals that have some serious girth to them, even with short traps!

Okay, now for some pics of S. leucophylla (various clones) Covington Co, AL taken 10/1/22:



Here's what I'm talking about:


some of these are probably albas. The white tops are quite white even if they don't color up to their fullest potential:


This is a proven alba clone, but doesn't look too alba-ish this year:


Love the girth and round mouths on these plants:






There are even albas with red bodies! This probably isn't one, but the top is pretty white:


Super beautiful clones up in this mix:
